title: Aytek Namitok — The “Voluntary” Adherence of Kabarda (Eastern Circassia) to Russia
lang: EN · TR · КАБ · РУС · DE · عر · АДЫ
description: Caucasian Review, Munich, 1956. A critique of the Soviet claim that Kabarda voluntarily joined Russia in 1557.

title: The Circassian Genocide
author: Walter Richmond
description: Rutgers University Press monograph on the Russo-Circassian War, the genocidal campaigns of 1821–22 and 1863–64, and five generations of diaspora up to the Sochi Olympics. Read via Project MUSE with library access, or purchase.

title: The Circassians: A Forgotten Genocide?
author: Stephen D. Shenfield
description: Chapter 7 of The Massacre in History, edited by Mark Levene and Penny Roberts (Berghahn Books, War and Genocide vol. 1). Examines the massacres and deportations of the 1860s and asks whether they amount to genocide. Available from the publisher.

title: Imperial Refuge: Resettlement of Muslims from Russia in the Ottoman Empire, 1860–1914
author: Vladimir Hamed-Troyansky · Stanford University
description: How the Ottoman state resettled about a million North Caucasian refugees in the Balkans, Anatolia and the Levant, based on archives in Turkey, Jordan, Bulgaria, Russia, Georgia and the UK. Free to download (CC BY-NC-ND) from the Stanford Digital Repository.

title: The Circassian Revival: A Quest for Recognition
author: Lars Funch Hansen · University of Copenhagen
description: Transnational Circassian mobilisation and memorialisation, and the campaign to have the 1864 exile recognised as genocide. The thesis is unpublished: request a copy through the University of Copenhagen library or from the author.

title: Civil War, Violence and Nationality from Empire to Nation State: The Circassians in Turkey (1918–1938)
author: Caner Yelbaşı · SOAS University of London
description: The Circassian diaspora in Anatolia from the last Ottoman years to the early Turkish Republic. Free to download (CC BY-NC-ND) from the SOAS research repository.

title: The First 'Circassian Exodus' to the Ottoman Empire (1858–1867), and the Ottoman Response
author: Sarah A. S. Isla Rosser-Owen · SOAS University of London
description: The arrival of Circassian refugees in Ottoman Black Sea ports and the Ottoman response, based on the reports of British consuls, journalists and other eyewitnesses.

title: Ukraine's and Georgia's Recognition of the Circassian Genocide: Strategic Engagement with North Caucasian Causes
author: Matthew Kelbaugh · Journal of Caucasian Studies 10 (16): 79–116
description: How Georgia (2011) and Ukraine have recognised the Circassian genocide, and what these recognitions mean for the politics of memory and for stateless peoples resisting Russian rule.

title: Position and Diplomatic Demarches of Great Britain in Connection with the Exodus of the Circassians to the Ottoman Empire in 1864
author: Georgy V. Chochiev · Caucasology no. 4: 73–89 · DOI 10.31143/2542-212X-2025-4-73-89
description: Based on British diplomatic correspondence: how the Foreign Office handled the mass exodus of 1863–64, and why London declined to act. Article in Russian with an English abstract.

title: Immigration and Settlement of Circassians in the Ottoman Empire on British Documents, 1857–1864
author: Musa Şaşmaz · OTAM 9: 331–366
description: A detailed reconstruction from Foreign Office files (FO 97/424, FO 881) of the expulsion, the refugee camps at Trabzon and Samsun, mortality at sea and the settlement of survivors across the Ottoman Empire.

title: Immigration and Settlement of Abkhazians in the Ottoman Empire on British Documents, 1864–67
author: Musa Şaşmaz
description: The sequel to the Circassian exodus: the removal of the Prince of Abkhazia, the forced emigration of 1867 and the separation of families, as recorded by British consuls.

title: The Struggle over the Circassian Genocide: Between Historical Recognition and Current Practicalities
author: Michael Geheran & Chen Bram · Clark University, CHGS Conference Proceedings
description: Paper from Clark University's Strassler Center for Holocaust and Genocide Studies on the politics of recognising the Circassian genocide.

title: The Russian Final Subjugation of Northwestern Caucasus: Colonial Atrocities and European Responsibilities
author: Irma Kreiten · University of Southampton
description: Paper presented at the Circassian Day in the European Parliament, Brussels, on Russian colonial policy and ethnic cleansing in the Northwest Caucasus and Europe's share of responsibility.
